clue.text: Perhaps a daughter will be contracted for clerical work?

parts.note: the word 'a' is an example of an article in grammar, the indefinite one

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a daughter will be taken on for office work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps a' tells you to think of what kind of word 'a' is: an indefinite article. An articled clerk is one bound by contract to train with a solicitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee solicitor's clerk was bound by articles of agreement, so being employed under such terms is to be articled.

clue.text: At risk of falling apart, court disaster

indicators.note: something falling apart breaks up, so the letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone at risk of collapse is inviting catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling apart' rearranges the letters of AT RISK OF.
explanation.definitionFit: To court disaster is to invite trouble, which is the idiom of behaving so as to deserve what comes.

clue.text: Very loud sailor drowning in booze becomes jovial

indicators.note: one thing drowning in another sits wholly inside it, so these letters go within the drink

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer, i.e. booze
FF is fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud
AB is an able-bodied seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor sinking a lot of drink grows cheerful and noisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drowning in' puts FFAB inside ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a friendly, good-humoured and easy-going manner.

clue.text: Injury obtained in country when crossing river

indicators.note: the country stretches across the river, so it encloses its letter

parts.note: Spain is a country

explanation.surface: Someone got hurt abroad while fording a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when crossing' puts R inside SPAIN; 'obtained in' only links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrenched ligament in a joint such as an ankle is a common injury.

clue.text: Trainer taking fellows on to one of Dartmoor's high spots

parts.note: fellows are men
a tor is a rocky hilltop, typical of Dartmoor, a moorland in Devon, England

explanation.surface: A coach takes a group of men up a hill on the moor.
explanation.walkthrough: Dartmoor is a moorland in south-west England dotted with tors, granite outcrops on hilltops.
explanation.definitionFit: A guide who coaches and advises a less experienced person is a trainer of sorts.

clue.text: Extracts from lecture, say, for linguistic classes

explanation.surface: Snippets from a talk are used to illustrate grammar categories.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, pieces of a speech; as a grammar term, noun, verb, adjective and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally sections of an address; in grammar the word classes such as noun, verb and adjective.

clue.text: Valuable material may come from a tues. Compiler!

indicators.note: the answer is said to arise out of these letters, so they are rearranged to produce it

explanation.surface: A setter boasts that something precious could emerge from a Tuesday puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may come from' rearranges the letters of A TUES COMPILER; the full stop and exclamation are just decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold, silver and platinum are prized substances, examples of costly material.

clue.text: Accommodation complex in nasty ghettoes in USA

indicators.note: nasty suggests something spoiled or rough, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Unpleasant American ghettoes are described as a cluster of homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges the letters of GHETTOES IN USA; the 'in' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A planned group of homes built together is a residential development.

clue.text: Faith makes you exist happily — in the past

parts.note: to exist is to be
lief is an old word meaning gladly or willingly

explanation.surface: Believing lets you live contentedly, in olden days at least.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the past' marks LIEF as archaic: 'I would as lief' meant 'I would as gladly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Trust or conviction in something is faith.

clue.text: Plant badly built huts behind a prison

indicators.note: one part placed behind another comes after it in the answer

parts.note: can is slang for prison

indicators.note: badly built means put together wrongly, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Shoddy shacks have been put up at the back of a jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' is the definition, not a verb. 'badly built' rearranges the hut letters, and 'behind' places that result after the prison piece. 'can' is American slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mediterranean shrub with spiny leaves, whose foliage decorates Corinthian columns, is a plant.

clue.text: Sphere of gold presented to bishop

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A golden ball is given to a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A globe, as in the monarch's regalia, is a sphere.

clue.text: Norm, about 15, may be a supporter of the church

indicators.note: about here means around, so these letters surround the cross-referenced answer

parts.note: par is the standard or norm
15 points to the answer of clue 15-down, which means bad

explanation.surface: A man named Norm, sick, may still be a stalwart of his parish.
explanation.walkthrough: Norm looks like a name but is the word for an average or standard. '15' borrows the answer of 15-down.
explanation.definitionFit: A staunch and prominent member is called a pillar of the church; literally a column holding up its roof.

clue.text: Bird to come down by bit of fence

parts.note: to land is to come down to earth
a rail is a horizontal bar of a fence

explanation.surface: A bird drops down beside a fence post.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for the corncrake, a bird of meadows.

clue.text: Expected lord to get rid of the king

indicators.note: getting rid of something removes it, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: a duke is a lord
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A nobleman is predicted to depose the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get rid of' takes K out of DUKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something anticipated at a set time, like a train or a baby, is expected.

clue.text: Stupid man finally involved experts

indicators.note: involved means intricate or tangled, so these letters are mixed up
finally takes the last letter of the word man

explanation.surface: A foolish man ended up embroiled with the specialists.
explanation.walkthrough: Take N, last of 'man', and with STUPID let 'involved' rearrange them.
explanation.definitionFit: Commentators consulted for authority on a subject are learned authorities.

clue.text: Jill's chucked Jack? Bad!

indicators.note: to chuck someone is to dump them, so this letter is removed

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Jill has dumped Jack, and it's awful!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jill's' is 'Jill has'; 'chucked' removes J, which is Jack in card games. Jack and Jill are the nursery-rhyme pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor in quality or harmful, as in ill effects, is bad.

clue.text: Omen about end of Romans seen in part of book

indicators.note: these letters are seen within the other word, so they go inside it

parts.note: a page is part of a book
re means about or concerning

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of Romans

explanation.surface: A portent is found concerning the conclusion of the Epistle to the Romans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' sets the 'about' letters plus the final S of 'Romans' inside the book part. Romans is also a book of the Bible, which adds to the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign that foretells something is an omen.

clue.text: North American flowing water about to descend on motorist

indicators.note: in a down answer, a part descending on another sits above it

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a motorist is a driver

explanation.surface: A North American river is about to come down on a car driver.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'to descend on' stacks the first piece above the second. The Red River runs along the Texas-Oklahoma border, and another flows north through Manitoba.
explanation.definitionFit: A river of the US South and another of Manitoba carry this name, so it is a North American watercourse.

clue.text: Harem exciting eg sailor

indicators.note: exciting means stirring up, so these letters are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: A harem thrills, for example, a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exciting' rearranges the letters of EG SAILOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The women's quarters of an Ottoman palace, or the women living there, is a harem.

clue.text: Something kept in part of hospital included in note

indicators.note: these letters are included within the other word, so they go inside it

parts.note: a memo is a note
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A souvenir from a hospital department is mentioned in a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included in' sets the hospital department inside the note. ENT stands for ear, nose and throat.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake retained as a reminder of a person or event is something kept.

clue.text: I am dead after short time, making sacrifice

indicators.note: one part coming after another is placed later in the answer

parts.note: I'm is short for I am
mo is short for moment, a short time
late means dead, as in the late king

explanation.surface: Someone says they will die after a moment, making a sacrifice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the word for dead last. 'making' only links the definition, which is the verb meaning to offer up.
explanation.definitionFit: To kill as an offering, especially by burning, is to sacrifice.

clue.text: Costume is not in fashion, though suitable

parts.note: out means no longer fashionable
fit means suitable

explanation.surface: A costume is old-fashioned but still appropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of clothes worn together is a costume.

clue.text: Priest's garment, one being worn in ancient Britain

parts.note: an alb is a white vestment worn by a priest
I is the Roman numeral one
on means being worn, as in having a coat on

explanation.surface: A priest's vestment, one in use in Britain of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being worn' looks like it wants a container, but it simply gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The old poetic name for Britain or England is used for the ancient island.

clue.text: Force middle of tum into garment

indicators.note: one part going into another sits inside it

parts.note: a dress is a garment

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letter of the word tum

explanation.surface: A tummy is being forced into a tight frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts U, the middle of 'tum', inside DRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Compulsion by threats or pressure is force.

clue.text: Farm animal going around ruin

indicators.note: turning around reverses direction, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep, a farm animal

explanation.surface: A farm animal on the loose wrecks everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going around' reverses RAM.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoil or damage something is to ruin it.

clue.text: Good person on a list that can be made known

parts.note: ST is short for saint, a good person
a table is a list of figures or items

explanation.surface: A virtuous person features on a register of names that can be revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' just means next to, so it joins the saint to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something capable of being stated or declared is able to be made public.

clue.text: Some starting early ready to be driven off?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people make an early start, ready to drive off.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'starting' into 'early'.
explanation.definitionFit: A car with a gear engaged is ready to move off, which is the motoring idiom.

clue.text: Risked being left for a train to run over

definitions.text: being left for a train to run over

explanation.surface: Someone gambled everything, like a victim tied to the tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: Laying something on the line is putting it at stake; read literally, it is placed on the railway track.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means staked or hazarded; the literal sense is placed on a railway track.
